1. Market Overview & Transaction Summary

This report analyzes 5,000 Air Jordan secondary-market transactions spanning from 2023-01-01 to 2025-09-27. The aggregate market shows an average resale price of $273.23 against an average retail price of $191.17, yielding a mean profit margin of $82.06 per transaction. Overall, 61.3% of all transactions sold above retail price.

Gross Market Summary: Total aggregate profit across all transactions: $410,290.56. 3,066 transactions (61.3%) were profitable; 1,934 (38.7%) sold at a loss relative to retail.

The profit margin distribution above shows a roughly bell-shaped curve centered near break-even, with a long right tail of high-profit transactions (collectible Deadstock pairs) and a left tail of losses on Used and less-desirable colorways. The mean ($82.06) sits modestly above zero, reflecting a market where resellers must be selective to consistently profit.

2. Performance by Shoe Model & Colorway

The chart above ranks every Air Jordan silhouette in the dataset by average profit margin. Models on the right (positive margin) consistently sell above retail; those on the left underperform. Volume (n) varies substantially — high-volume models offer more reliable signals, while low-volume outliers should be interpreted cautiously.

Model-Level Finding: The number of distinct models and their profit spread highlights significant dispersion in resale performance. A reseller's model selection is the single most impactful sourcing decision. High-volume models with consistently positive margins represent the safest sourcing targets.

3. Impact of Shoe Condition on Resale Value

Condition is the second-strongest determinant of resale value after model selection. The three panels above quantify the premium gap:

  • Deadstock (Brand New): Average profit of $264.01 with a resale-to-retail ratio of 2.38x. 100.0% of Deadstock pairs sell above retail.
  • VNDS (Very Near Deadstock): Average profit of $37.62 with a resale-to-retail ratio of 1.20x. 83.0% of VNDS pairs sell above retail.
  • Used: Average loss of $57.66 with a resale-to-retail ratio of 0.70x. Only 0.0% of Used pairs sell above retail.
Sourcing Implication: The Deadstock-to-Used premium gap is approximately $321.67, meaning a Deadstock pair commands roughly 3.4x the return multiple of an equivalent Used pair. For resellers with access to Deadstock inventory, the premium justifies the higher acquisition cost. For budget-focused flippers, VNDS represents a middle-ground with moderate profit potential and lower capital requirements.

6. Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations

Core Finding: The Air Jordan resale market is segmented — profitability is concentrated in specific models, colorways, and conditions, while a substantial portion of transactions clear at or below retail. Success requires disciplined sourcing and channel selection, not broad-based buying.

Sourcing: Prioritize Deadstock of High-Premium Models

Deadstock (Brand New) inventory of the top-performing shoe models achieves average profit margins well above $50.00. These models have consistent buyer demand and strong brand equity. Allocate the majority of sourcing budget here. The average resale-to-retail ratio for Deadstock is 2.38x — meaning every dollar spent at retail returns roughly 2.38x in resale.

Channel Strategy: Match Product to Platform

List Deadstock pairs on channels with the highest average resale prices and profit margins, even if inventory takes slightly longer to move. For VNDS and Used, prioritize faster-moving channels to minimize holding costs. The profit-velocity scatter chart above provides a visual map for this matching exercise. The fastest channel clears inventory 4.4x faster than the slowest.

Inventory Management: 30-Day Target Window

The overall average days in inventory is 22.5 days. Transactions exceeding this threshold tie up capital and degrade annualized returns. Set a 30-day target for most inventory; consider discounting or channel-switching for items sitting beyond 45 days. VNDS inventory tends to clear faster than Deadstock (averaging 21.7 days vs. 23.0 days for Deadstock).

Timing: Buy in Low-Volume Periods, Sell into Strength

Monthly transaction volumes show identifiable seasonal patterns. Acquire inventory during volume troughs when seller competition is lower and prices dip. List during volume peaks — holiday seasons and major sneaker release windows — when buyer activity and willingness to pay premiums are highest. The seasonal breakdown table quantifies these window-specific profit differentials.

Risk Management: Avoid Below-Retail Colorways Entirely

The bottom-tier colorways (averaging negative margins of $69.34 to $83.19) consistently underperform across all conditions and channels. These represent deadweight loss — capital tied up in inventory that predictably sells at a loss. Exclude these from sourcing portfolios. Only 61.3% of all transactions are profitable, underscoring the importance of selective buying.

Portfolio Diversification: Model Mix Matters

Spread sourcing across 3-4 top-performing models rather than concentrating in a single silhouette. This hedges against model-specific demand shifts while maintaining exposure to the highest-margin segments. Models with the strongest profit profiles are clearly identifiable in the model performance chart (Section 2).
